text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Hosted runtime 'prod-hosted-us-east-1' reporting kvcache memory spike and OOMs. Multiple nodes showing oom_kill, elevated 5xx on /v1/generate. Pager routed to oncall-sre. Incident-id: 2148-kvcache-spike.

alice (oncall-sre): acked. I'm on it. seeing a big jump in kvcache size on gpu-runner-7/8 — usage jumped from ~40GB to ~180GB in ~6m. 5xx rate for rdx-2.1 generation endpoints up from 0.2% -> 6.3%.

brad (eng-runtime): looking. early signs point to continuous-batching prefetch loop: prefetch window multiplier appears to have applied recursively for very long contexts. I can see a config rollout from ~20m ago (deploy-bot shows `cbatch/prefetch:v2.4` went live).

dinesh (eng-ml): we saw a handful of very long prompts this morning from a customer test harness — one request kept appending context segments (estimated ~80k tokens). continuous batching held KV windows open and prefetch pulled many prefixes. explains runaway cache growth.

carla (prod-support): heads up — three enterprise tenants reported timeouts; two opened support tickets. I'm drafting a status note for affected accounts.

alice (oncall-sre): mitigation plan: 1) disable prefetch for hosted runtime to stop new growth, 2) shrink active batch window sizes on serving nodes, 3) trigger async eviction sweep. Brad — can you flip flag and push a hotfix?

brad (eng-runtime): on it. executing hotpatch to disable prefetch + reduce batch window. applying change via control plane now. command: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/feature-flags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"continuous_batching": {"prefetch_enabled": false, "max_window_tokens": 4096}}'
```

deploy-bot: deployment cbatch-prefetch-hotfix started by brad (eng-runtime) — rollouts to prod-hosted-us-east-1 (canary 10% -> 100%).

brad (eng-runtime): canary applied to 10% — monitoring metrics. beginning eviction sweep on nodes with >120GB kv usage. running: `kvcachectl evict --threshold 120GB --mode=aggressive`

alice (oncall-sre): good. routing rule: temporarily reject requests with prompt length > 20k tokens at edge for hosted tier to protect runtime. patch applied to API gateway rule set.

carla (prod-support): customer comms: emailed three affected accounts with mitigation steps + ETA. asking for any impacted logs they can share. Erin - can you coordinate direct outreach for the largest account?

erin (customer-success): on it. scheduling call with account CSP in 15m; will provide status and workarounds (limit long-prompt batch, retry guidance).

brad (eng-runtime): hotfix fully rolled out at +13m. prefetch flag: false across cluster. batch window reduced. early telemetry: kvcache growth rate flattening, oom events ceased on patched nodes. 5xx rate dropping; now 1.1%.

dinesh (eng-ml): confirming that the specific long-context test that triggered growth had a loop producing repeated prefixes that multiplied prefetch fanout. adding prompt-length guard in model-serving layer to avoid internal loops.

alice (oncall-sre): next steps: 1) keep prefetch disabled for 2h while we watch, 2) run full eviction sweep and reclaim memory, 3) rollback cbatch/prefetch:v2.4 rollout (it caused config regression), 4) capture heap dumps and logs for postmortem. Brad, can you own the rollback?

brad (eng-runtime): I will roll back the cbatch/prefetch:v2.4 change and open a PR for a safe prefetch backoff. rollback started. commit: `revert: cbatch/prefetch:v2.4 (sha: a1b2c3d4)`

deploy-bot: rollback cbatch/prefetch:v2.4 completed.

alice (oncall-sre): monitoring 30m after rollback — memory on nodes trend down to normal, 5xx back to baseline ~0.3%. no new oom_kill.

carla (prod-support): support tickets updated. customers acknowledged the fix; one requested token-level breakdown and we promised follow-up postmortem.

erin (customer-success): call with biggest account done. they were generating long-sessions — suggested temporary quota and recommended batching best-practices. they appreciated rapid response.

brad (eng-runtime): quick root cause summary: prefetch backoff logic failed to cap fanout during pathological long-context sequences introduced by a customer test harness + a newly rolled config that increased default prefetch multiplier. combination led to exponential KV cache growth and eventual OOMs.

dinesh (eng-ml): mitigation ideas to add to runbook: - hard cap on prefetch depth per request, - token-count guardrail rejecting or truncating >50k tokens, - backpressure signal from runtime to API to limit concurrent long-context requests.

alice (oncall-sre): severity classified as Sev2. Postmortem owner: brad (eng-runtime). I'm handing off incident to brad for 2h post-ops monitoring. If anything spikes, ping me. :thumbsup:

brad (eng-runtime): taking handoff. I'll file the postmortem and include timeline, metrics, and the proposed runbook changes. planned follow-ups: add alert for kvcache growth rate > 20GB/min, prefetch fanout anomaly detector, and a safe rollout checklist for batching config changes.

carla (prod-support): note for PMs/product — consider docs + quickstart guidance on safe prompt sizes and long-session patterns. ops impact: temporary throttle applied to hosted tier; dedicated customers unaffected.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: 2148-kvcache-spike — mitigation applied, root cause identified, recovery verified. Follow-up: postmortem in #postmortems in 48h.

brad (eng-runtime): closing thread for now. will post postmortem link here when ready. thanks everyone for fast coordination. :coffee:
